note: Attacker-controlled IRC message tags are isolated from the incoming line and passed onward as the tags string.
The parser forwards the extracted tags pointer into the message-tag parser when tags are present.
The tags string is split into key/value fields, preserving a lone tag escape sequence inside a field.
Each field is split on '=', so a tag with no '=' leaves kv[1] NULL while a tag with a trailing backslash keeps the escape character in the value slot when present.

code: for (; *tmp != '\0'; tmp++, tag++) { if (*tmp == '\') { tmp++; switch (*tmp) { ... default: *tag = *tmp; break; } } else { *tag = *tmp; } }
note: A lone trailing backslash advances tmp past the string terminator and the loop does not stop on that escape, causing incorrect parsing behavior in the tag value.
